Use when the user wants a RAG system, semantic search index or chat-over-documents feature reviewed, or asks why retrieval quality is poor before deciding what to change.

agents.name: react-reviewer
agents.description: React and Next.js change reviewer that reads a diff in its own context and reports verified defects - Rules of Hooks violations, effects with missing or wrong dependencies and no cleanup, stale closures, unstable or index keys, state mirrored from props, "use client"/"use server" boundary leaks of secrets or server data, unprotected Server Actions, and accessibility regressions - without editing files. Use when the user wants a React, JSX/TSX or Next.js App Router change, branch or pull request reviewed before merging.

agents.name: refactor-cleaner
agents.description: Removes dead code from a repository, including unreferenced functions and files, unused exports, unused package dependencies and duplicated helper functions, but only after gathering evidence that nothing uses each item, and runs the tests after every single deletion. Use when the user wants to prune dead code, drop unused dependencies, shrink a bloated codebase, or consolidate copy-pasted utility functions.

agents.name: ruby-build-resolver
agents.description: Repair subagent that gets a broken Ruby environment loading again by fixing Bundler resolution conflicts, lockfile platform mismatches, gem native extension compile failures (nokogiri, pg, mysql2, ffi, psych), LoadError and load path problems, and Ruby version mismatches with the smallest possible change, then re-runs the failing command as proof. Use when bundle install or bundle exec fails, a gem will not build its C extension, Ruby raises cannot load such file, or the app refuses to boot after a Ruby or gem upgrade.

agents.name: ruby-reviewer
agents.description: Read-only review subagent for Ruby and Rails diffs that hunts NoMethodError on nil, rescue clauses that swallow everything, N+1 queries and missing eager loading, risky metaprogramming such as send or constantize on user input, unpermitted mass assignment, and SQL, shell or YAML injection, then returns verified findings ranked by severity. Use when the user wants a Ruby branch, pull request or set of changed .rb files checked before merge, or asks whether a Rails change introduces nil crashes, query explosions or injection holes.

agents.name: rust-build-resolver
agents.description: Repairs failing cargo build, cargo check and cargo test compilation by reading rustc error codes and fixing borrow checker conflicts, lifetime mismatches, unsatisfied trait bounds, missing feature flags and conflicting dependency versions with the smallest diff, then re-running cargo to prove the build is green. Use when a Rust project no longer compiles, rustc reports errors such as E0502, E0499, E0382, E0277 or E0308, or a Cargo.lock or dependency upgrade broke the build.

agents.name: rust-reviewer
agents.description: Rust-specific change reviewer that hunts for unwrap and expect outside tests, reachable panics and indexing, unsound or undocumented unsafe blocks, blocking calls and std Mutex guards held across await in tokio code, needless clones, and swallowed or stringly-typed errors, then returns verified findings without touching files. Use when a Rust diff, crate or pull request needs a language-aware review before merge, or when the user wants a second opinion on unsafe or async Rust code.

agents.name: security-reviewer
agents.description: Isolated security pass over a diff, branch or pull request that traces untrusted input to where it is used and reports only exploitable problems - leaked secrets, SQL, shell and template injection, path traversal and SSRF, missing or broken authorization (IDOR), weak input validation, and sensitive data in responses or logs - each ranked by severity with an attack scenario and a fix, never modifying the code. Use when the user wants a vulnerability check of their change delegated to a subagent, a security gate before merging, or an independent look at whether a new endpoint or handler can be abused.

agents.name: silent-failure-hunter
agents.description: Read-only auditor that searches a diff, module or service for places where failures vanish without a trace, such as empty or catch-all exception handlers, discarded error returns, unawaited promises, fallback values that mask a broken dependency, and error paths with no log or metric, then reports each with its concrete consequence. Use when the user suspects errors are being hidden, asks why something fails with no logs, or wants a change audited for swallowed exceptions before merging.

agents.name: solidity-reviewer
agents.description: Read-only Solidity diff reviewer that inspects changed contracts in its own context for reentrancy through external calls made before state updates, privileged or initializer functions left without access control, low-level calls whose return value is ignored, unsafe downcasts and rounding that favours the caller, storage layout collisions between proxy implementation versions, and state changes that emit no event, then returns line-anchored findings it has traced or proven with a test, never editing files. Use when a pull request or commit touches .sol files, before merging contract changes, or when the user asks whether a Solidity change is safe to ship.

agents.name: spec-reviewer
agents.description: Requirements-conformance reviewer that compares a finished change against the ticket, task or spec it was supposed to satisfy, reading the real code and tests instead of believing the implementer's summary. Reports requirements that are missing or only partly met, unrequested additions, and requirements that were misunderstood, each backed by file:line evidence, and returns PASS or a ranked gap list without editing anything or judging style. Use when someone asks whether a branch, commit range or pull request actually delivers what its ticket or plan task specified, or as the scope gate before a code-quality review.

agents.name: swift-build-resolver
agents.description: Repairs failing Swift and Xcode builds with the smallest diff, working through compiler errors, Swift 6 strict concurrency diagnostics such as non-Sendable sends and actor-isolated access, SwiftPM dependency resolution and Package.resolved conflicts, and build settings like SWIFT_VERSION or search paths, then re-runs the failing build to prove it passes. Use when swift build, swift test or xcodebuild fails, after a toolchain, Xcode or Swift 6 upgrade breaks compilation, or when SwiftPM cannot resolve or fetch packages. Not for code signing or provisioning problems.

agents.name: swift-reviewer
agents.description: Read-only Swift code reviewer that inspects a diff for crash-prone force unwraps and try!, retain cycles in escaping closures, actor isolation mistakes and Sendable violations, UIKit or SwiftUI state touched off the main actor, and swallowed or misrouted errors, then returns verified findings ranked by severity. Use when the user wants a Swift or iOS/macOS pull request checked before merge, asks whether a change could leak memory or race, or wants a second opinion on Swift concurrency code.

agents.name: task-implementer
agents.description: Focused build subagent that carries out exactly one task from an implementation plan, from the full task text and context handed to it. Asks its questions before touching anything, works test-first (a failing test seen to fail for the stated reason, then the smallest code that passes), stays inside the task's file list, commits, reviews its own diff, and reports with a fixed DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, NEEDS_CONTEXT or BLOCKED status instead of guessing past a problem. Use when a controller running a plan task by task needs one task built in a fresh context, or when the user hands over a single, fully specified plan task to implement.

agents.name: typescript-build-resolver
agents.description: Repairs failing TypeScript and JavaScript builds with the smallest diff, working through tsc type errors, "Cannot find module" and module resolution failures, ESM/CJS interop errors, bundler (Vite, webpack, esbuild, tsup) failures and broken or mismatched npm/pnpm dependencies, then re-runs the failing command to prove it passes. Use when tsc, npm run build, a bundler or CI type-check is red and the user wants it green again.

agents.name: typescript-reviewer
agents.description: TypeScript and JavaScript diff reviewer that hunts type holes (any, unsafe casts, non-null assertions, ts-ignore), floating or unhandled promises, async races, ESM/CommonJS import breakage and runtime bugs the compiler cannot see, then returns verified findings without touching files. Use when a TS/JS change, branch or pull request needs a language-aware review before it is committed or merged.

agents.name: ui-auditor
agents.description: Visual quality auditor for implemented frontend screens that works in its own context, reads the components and styles and, when a browser is available, the rendered pages, then scores six areas (layout and spacing, typography, colour and contrast, interaction states, responsive behaviour, and content, empty and error states) from 1 to 4 with file:line or screenshot evidence and returns the highest-value fixes, without editing anything. Use when someone wants built UI graded for finish and consistency before a release or design sign-off, asks why a screen looks off, or wants a scored UI report rather than a WCAG audit or a new visual direction.

agents.name: vue-reviewer
agents.description: Read-only reviewer for Vue 3 and Nuxt diffs that hunts for state which silently stops being reactive, watchers and listeners never torn down, props or store state mutated from a child, server and client rendering that disagree, and Nuxt data fetched twice or secrets exposed through public runtime config, then returns verified findings with file and line. Use when the user wants a Vue or Nuxt pull request, branch or uncommitted change checked before merge.

commands.name: aside
commands.description: Answer a quick side question without changing files or losing the thread of the current task, then pick the task up where it was.

commands.name: brainstorm
commands.description: Turn a rough idea into an approved design before any code is written, asking one question at a time and comparing approaches.

commands.name: build-fix
commands.description: Fix the current build, compile or type-check failure with the smallest change, routed to the build resolver for that language.

commands.name: campaign
commands.description: Plan a marketing campaign: audience, positioning, channels, messages, calendar, budget split and success metrics.

commands.name: capture
commands.description: Park an idea, todo or seed in the project backlog in one line without starting work on it, then carry on with the current task.

commands.name: changelog
commands.description: Write changelog entries for the changes since the last release tag, grouped by type, with breaking changes called out first.

commands.name: checkpoint
commands.description: Save a restorable snapshot of the working tree after running the project's checks, without committing or changing anything, or list and restore earlier ones.

commands.name: codemap
commands.description: Write or refresh a short architecture map of the codebase (entry points, modules, data flow, commands) at docs/CODEMAP.md, so agents can orient without reading everything.

commands.name: commit
commands.description: Write a Conventional Commits message for the staged changes, show it, and commit only after the user confirms.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Find the root cause of a bug, failing test or unexpected behaviour by evidence before proposing or making any fix.

commands.name: deps-audit
commands.description: Audit the project's dependencies for known vulnerabilities, abandoned or risky packages and licence problems, and report fixes by severity.

commands.name: developer-profile
commands.description: Build a short working-style profile of you from your own local agent session logs, read-only and on this machine only, then show it and write it to AGENTS.md or a profile file only if you approve.

commands.name: dual-review
commands.description: Two independent reviewers, optionally on different models or providers, review the same change against one rubric; fix and repeat until both approve or the round limit is hit, then report disagreements.

commands.name: epic-decompose
commands.description: Break a feature or epic into small, independently shippable issues with acceptance criteria, and create them in GitHub, Jira or Linear after approval.

commands.name: explain
commands.description: Explain how a piece of code or a flow works, tracing it through the codebase with file:line references, without changing anything.

commands.name: feature-dev
commands.description: Build a feature end to end: plan it, implement it test-first, review it and verify it, stopping for approval between stages.

commands.name: finish-branch
commands.description: Finish the current branch - run the checks, confirm the base, then merge locally, open a pull request, keep it or discard it, with cleanup and no force-push or deletion without consent.

commands.name: fix-bug
commands.description: Fix a reported bug by reproducing it as a failing regression test, finding the root cause, making the smallest fix, verifying, reviewing the diff and offering a commit.

commands.name: fix-findings
commands.description: Work through review or audit findings one at a time, confirming each is real, fixing it with a regression test, verifying and committing per fix. Supports --max <n> and --dry-run.

commands.name: forensics
commands.description: Read-only post-mortem of a multi-session piece of work that went wrong, rebuilding the timeline from git history and plan, state and handoff files to find where it diverged and how to recover, without changing anything.

commands.name: hookify
commands.description: Turn a rule the agent must never break into an enforced hook: write it in the portable Kete Loom hook format, test it with cases, and show how to register it.

commands.name: i18n-check
commands.description: Check the current UI changes for internationalisation problems such as hard-coded strings, concatenation, plurals, and date or currency formatting.

commands.name: issue-sync
commands.description: Bring tracked issues in line with the work: find the issues this branch or PR addresses and propose status updates, comments and links, applying them after approval.

commands.name: jira
commands.description: Work with Jira from the agent: find, read, create or update issues with JQL and transitions, asking before any change.

commands.name: learn
commands.description: Turn a lesson from this session into a lasting project rule, in AGENTS.md or a Kete Loom rule, so future sessions don't repeat the mistake.

commands.name: lint-agent-config
commands.description: Lint a project's agent setup (AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, skills, agents, commands, rules, hooks, MCP configs, plugin manifests) for broken references, invalid frontmatter, bloat, conflicts and risky settings.

commands.name: loom
commands.description: Find the Kete Loom skills, agents, commands, rules, hooks or MCP servers that fit what you are doing, and show how to install them.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a bounded autonomous loop toward a goal, with a stop condition, a budget and a check after every iteration.

commands.name: model-route
commands.description: Recommend which model tier to use for a task (fast, balanced or most capable), weighing complexity, risk and cost, and say how to switch in this host.

commands.name: onboard
commands.description: Get oriented in an unfamiliar codebase: what it does, how it is laid out, how to build, test and run it, and where to start.

commands.name: orchestrate
commands.description: Split a large task into independent pieces, run them in parallel subagents, then verify and merge their results.

commands.name: plan-feature
commands.description: Turn a feature request into a step-by-step implementation plan with files to touch, risks and tests, without writing code.

commands.name: postmortem
commands.description: Write a blameless postmortem for an incident, with timeline, impact, root cause, contributing factors and owned action items.

commands.name: pr
commands.description: Open a pull request for the current branch: check it is ready, write the title and description, push, and create the PR, asking before anything leaves the machine.

commands.name: pr-describe
commands.description: Draft a pull request title and description for the current branch from its commits and diff against the base branch.

commands.name: prd
commands.description: Draft a product requirements document for a feature, with problem, users, requirements, success metrics and open questions.

commands.name: production-readiness
commands.description: Audit a service before launch for health checks, observability, rollback, backups, limits, secrets and runbooks, and return a go/no-go list with evidence.

commands.name: progress
commands.description: Show where the project stands from its .planning/ files, git and handoff notes, and name the single next action, stopping at hard gates such as unverified phases or open blockers.

commands.name: project-init
commands.description: Set a repository up for coding agents: write or improve AGENTS.md, install the Kete Loom packs for its stack, and fix what the readiness audit flags.

commands.name: refactor-clean
commands.description: Find and remove dead code, unused exports and unused dependencies, verifying with the build and tests after each removal.

commands.name: repo-triage
commands.description: Triage a GitHub repository's open issues and pull requests against its own templates and CONTRIBUTING rules, proposing labels, comments and closes in batches that are applied only after approval.

commands.name: resume-session
commands.description: Resume work from the latest session handoff note, checking it against the repository before taking the next step.

commands.name: revert-work
commands.description: Safely undo the commits of a task, phase or the last few changes with git revert, after checking later commits that depend on them and getting confirmation; never resets or force-pushes.

commands.name: review
commands.description: Review the current changes for bugs, risky patterns and missing tests, routed to the reviewer for the language that changed.

commands.name: rules-review
commands.description: Review recent local agent session logs, read-only, against AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, rules and installed skills; report broken, missing, stale and untriggered guidance, and edit only what you approve.

commands.name: save-session
commands.description: Save a handoff note recording the current goal, progress, decisions and next steps so a later session can resume.

commands.name: security-scan
commands.description: Scan the current change for vulnerabilities, leaked secrets and unsafe dependencies, and report findings by severity.

commands.name: sessions
commands.description: List the session handoff notes in this repository with their branch, date and next step, and tidy up ones that are finished, only with the user's go-ahead.

commands.name: skill-create
commands.description: Create a new Agent Skill for a repeated workflow, to the Kete Loom spec, with trigger evals, and check it before use.

commands.name: skill-review
commands.description: Review the skill observation log and turn open findings into staged, approved changes to skills, rules, hooks or instructions files, one decision at a time.

commands.name: tdd
commands.description: Implement the requested change test-first, writing one failing test, the smallest code to pass it, then refactoring, step by step.

commands.name: test-coverage
commands.description: Find untested behaviour in the current change and add focused tests for it, then show the coverage before and after.

commands.name: threat-model
commands.description: Produce a threat model for a feature or system, with assets, trust boundaries, data flows, STRIDE threats and ranked mitigations.

commands.name: uat
commands.description: Run user acceptance testing with the user on the current phase, feature or ticket, one check at a time, and save the results to a UAT file.

commands.name: update-docs
commands.description: Update the README, API docs, changelog and code comments that the current change made stale, without touching unrelated docs.

commands.name: usage-report
commands.description: Summarise token usage and estimated cost per session, project and model from local agent session logs (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kete Code), read-only.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify the current changes by running the project's build, lint, type-check and tests, then report pass or fail.

rules.name: cpp
rules.description: Always-on rules for modern C++ code, covering ownership and RAII, undefined behaviour, bounds and lifetimes, concurrency, headers, and sanitizer-backed build and test checks.

rules.name: csharp
rules.description: Always-on rules for C# and .NET code, covering nullable reference types, async and await, disposal, exceptions, data access safety, and build and test checks.

rules.name: dart
rules.description: Always-on rules for Dart and Flutter code, covering null safety, async, widget lifecycle, analysis, formatting and tests.

rules.name: fsharp
rules.description: Always-on rules for F# code, covering immutability, discriminated unions and exhaustive matching, Option and Result, async and task code, .NET interop, and checks.

rules.name: git
rules.description: Always-on git hygiene rules for agents, covering small focused commits, Conventional Commits messages, keeping secrets and generated files out, safe pushing and never rewriting shared history.

rules.name: go
rules.description: Always-on rules for Go files, covering formatting, vet, error handling, context, goroutine and resource lifetimes, and concurrency safety.

rules.name: java
rules.description: Always-on rules for Java files, covering build tooling, null handling, exceptions, resources, concurrency and injection safety.

rules.name: kotlin
rules.description: Always-on rules for Kotlin code, covering null safety, sealed types, coroutines and structured concurrency, Java interop, and build and test checks.

rules.name: perl
rules.description: Always-on rules for modern Perl 5 code, covering strict and warnings, lexical scope, safe open and system calls, untrusted input, SQL, encoding and tests.

rules.name: php
rules.description: Always-on rules for modern PHP 8 code, covering strict types, typed signatures, input handling, SQL, errors, Composer and tests.

rules.name: python
rules.description: Always-on rules for Python 3 files, covering environments, type hints, exceptions, resource handling, untrusted input and the project's own tooling.

rules.name: ruby
rules.description: Always-on rules for Ruby code, covering style, nil handling, exceptions, unsafe input, Bundler, Rails safety and tests.

rules.name: rust
rules.description: Always-on rules for Rust files, covering cargo tooling, error handling, panics, unsafe code, async and dependency hygiene.

rules.name: security
rules.description: Always-on secure coding rules for any language, covering input validation, injection, authorization, least privilege, deserialisation, dependencies and keeping secrets and personal data out of logs.

rules.name: swift
rules.description: Always-on rules for Swift code, covering optionals, value types, error handling, Swift concurrency and actors, memory and retain cycles, and build and test checks.

rules.name: testing
rules.description: Always-on rules for writing and running tests in any language, covering behaviour-focused tests, failing tests first for bugs, determinism, isolation, speed and running the suite before finishing.

rules.name: typescript
rules.description: Always-on rules for TypeScript and JavaScript files, covering type safety, untrusted input, async errors, modules and the project's own tooling.

rules.name: use-skills
rules.description: Always-on rule to check for an installed skill, agent or command that fits a task before starting it, say which one is used, and follow its steps rather than working from memory.

hooks.name: block-dangerous-commands
hooks.description: Stops the agent before it runs shell commands that destroy data or systems, such as rm -rf on / or your home folder, force-pushing main, wiping disks, piping curl into a shell, dropping databases or auto-approved terraform destroy.

hooks.name: block-foreground-servers
hooks.description: Stops the agent from starting a dev server or file watcher in the foreground, where it never exits and hangs the agent's shell, and tells it to run it in the background with output going to a log.

hooks.name: block-no-verify
hooks.description: Stops the agent from skipping the project's git hooks with git commit --no-verify, -n, HUSKY=0, SKIP= or a swapped core.hooksPath, so pre-commit checks keep running.

hooks.name: block-secret-reads
hooks.description: Stops the agent from printing or copying secrets files into the conversation through shell commands, such as cat .env, git show HEAD:.env or reading SSH keys and cloud credentials, while still letting it load them with source or --env-file.

hooks.name: block-unfinished-stubs
hooks.description: When the agent says it is done, checks the lines its uncommitted changes add to code and sends it back once if they leave TODOs, "not implemented" stubs, or focused (.only) or skipped tests behind.

hooks.name: capture-lessons
hooks.description: Once per session, when the agent finishes with changes in the repository, asks it to propose up to three reusable lessons from the session for /learn, saving nothing unless you approve.

hooks.name: context-monitor
hooks.description: Watches how full the agent's context window is after each tool call and warns the agent itself, once at 70% and again at 85%, to save its progress in a handoff note before compaction loses the details.

hooks.name: format-on-edit
hooks.description: After the agent edits a file, formats it with the formatter the project already uses (Biome or Prettier, Ruff or Black, gofmt, rustfmt), so agent changes match the project's style.

hooks.name: guard-file-truncation
hooks.description: Stops the first whole-file write that would cut an existing file of 40 or more lines to under half its length, which usually means the agent read only part of it, and lets a deliberate rewrite through on the second try.

hooks.name: guard-prompt-injection
hooks.description: Stops the agent from writing planted instructions, such as "ignore previous instructions", hidden Unicode or "don't tell the user", into AGENTS.md, rules, skills, agent files or .planning/, where every later session would obey them.

hooks.name: guard-secrets
hooks.description: Stops the agent from writing API keys, tokens, passwords, connection strings or private keys into files, using the same rules as the security-review secret scanner.

hooks.name: load-session-context
hooks.description: At the start of each session, tells the agent the current branch, how many uncommitted changes there are, and the latest session handoff note, so it picks up where the last session stopped.

hooks.name: notify-on-stop
hooks.description: Shows a desktop notification when the agent finishes its turn, so you can switch away during long tasks and come back when it is your move.

hooks.name: protect-files
hooks.description: Stops the agent from editing files that should never be hand-edited, such as .env files with secrets, package lockfiles, anything inside .git, and private keys.

hooks.name: protect-lint-config
hooks.description: Stops the agent from editing existing linter, formatter and type-checker configs, so it fixes the code that breaks a rule instead of weakening or switching off the rule.

hooks.name: read-before-edit
hooks.description: Stops the first edit of each existing file in a session and tells the agent to read the file and search for its callers first, so changes are grounded in the real code rather than a guess.

hooks.name: scan-read-injection
hooks.description: After the agent reads a file, fetches a web page or runs a web search, warns it when the content contains text aimed at an AI, such as "ignore previous instructions", fake system prompts or hidden Unicode, so it treats the content as data rather than orders.

hooks.name: stay-in-worktree
hooks.description: When the agent works in a linked git worktree, stops it from editing files outside that worktree, such as the main checkout or another worktree reached through an absolute path or ../, so parallel branches don't leak into each other.

hooks.name: validate-commit-message
hooks.description: In repositories that enforce Conventional Commits with commitlint or commitizen, stops the agent from committing with a message like "updated stuff" and has it rewrite the subject as type(scope): subject first.

hooks.name: verify-before-stop
hooks.description: When the agent says it is done, runs the project's own lint and type-check commands if files changed, and sends it back to fix any failure instead of letting it finish with broken code.
